title: SEAL: Towards Safe Autonomous Driving via Skill-Enabled Adversary Learning for Closed-Loop Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: No user-facing control; the designer fixes a learned criticality objective (predicted collision closeness and induced ego behavior deviation) that ranks candidate adversary trajectories.

control_mechanism.value: Learned score network ranks 32 candidate adversary paths; best path gives goals for a reactive hierarchical policy that picks skills from an adversarial prior in a VAE skill space.

base_model.value: Pretrained DenseTNT candidate generator, VectorNet-style score network, ReSkill-style skill VAE with separate benign and adversarial prior networks.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset; WOMD-Normal (500 scenarios, 400 train, 100 eval) and WOMD-SafeShift-Hard; MetaDrive simulator with IDM demonstrations.

metrics.value: Ego Success, Crash and Out of Road rates; realism meta-metric from Wasserstein distances on adversary yaw rate, acceleration, out-of-road; collision velocity, head-on and severe head-on rates.

controllability_evidence.value: Not a controllability test. SEAL-trained ego policies average a 21.5% increase in Success rate over the top baseline in each setting; ablations show learned objective and skill policy both needed.

stated_limitations.value: Finer-grained metrics in the objective could enable more adaptive, controllable generation beyond safety criticality; realism metrics at skill level could be improved.

notes: Adversarial perturbation for closed-loop ego training; controllability of generated scenarios is not the paper's goal, so control_family set to other.
